problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡y}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡y}.$ The partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $y$ is given by

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂y}=\frac{h(x,y)}{(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡y)^{2}}.
$$

Find the function $h(x,y).$

activity_context.topic_title: Computing Partial Derivatives Using the Rules of Differentiation

examples.problem: For the function $f(x,y) = \dfrac{4x-y}{x+y^2},$ evaluate $\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x}$ at the point $(2,-1).$
examples.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the quotient rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{4x-y}{x+{y}^{2}}) & =\frac{\frac{∂}{∂x}(4x-y)\cdot (x+{y}^{2})-(4x-y)\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x+{y}^{2})}{{(x+{y}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4\cdot (x+{y}^{2})-(4x-y)\cdot 1}{{(x+{y}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4x+4{y}^{2}-4x+y}{{(x+{y}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4{y}^{2}+y}{{(x+{y}^{2})}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(2,-1)\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}{|}_{(2,-1)} & =\frac{4(-1)^{2}+(-1)}{{(2+{(-1)}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4-1}{{3}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: For the function $f(x,y)=x\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)+x\sqrt{y},$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ at the point $(\frac{1}{4},4).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the sum and constant multiple rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)+x\sqrt{y}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy))+\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\sqrt{y}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy))+\sqrt{y}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the product, the chain, and the constant multiple rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy))+\sqrt{y}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x) & =(\frac{∂}{∂x}(x)\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)+x\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)))+\sqrt{y}\cdot (1) \\  & =(1\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)+x\cdot \frac{1}{xy}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(xy))+\sqrt{y} \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)+\frac{1}{y}\cdot y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x))+\sqrt{y} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)+1+\sqrt{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(\frac{1}{4},4):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}{|}_{(1/4,4)} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{4}\cdot 4)+1+\sqrt{4} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)+1+2 \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$
